passage:
A supermarket introduced self-checkout machines. Some customers liked paying quickly. Others struggled with fruit codes, coupons, or machine errors.
Workers did not disappear. Their jobs changed. They helped with machines, solved problems, checked age-restricted items, and guided customers.
A student working part-time there said the hardest part was not the technology. It was calming frustrated people.
The store learned that automation shifts human work rather than simply removing it.
Machines can scan items, but they cannot easily handle confusion, embarrassment, or anger. In a modern store, human service may become less visible but more important.
